title_en: Chongqing Suote Salt and Chemical Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Xinwanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over land use right transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. According to Article 191 of the Property Law of the PRC and Article 49 of the Security Law of the PRC, during the mortgage period, if the mortgagor transfers the mortgaged property, he/she shall notify the mortgagee and obtain the mortgagee's consent; otherwise, the transfer shall be invalid. However, Article 191 of the Property Law of the PRC and Article 67 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the PRC also provide that if the mortgaged property is transferred without notification or without the mortgagee's consent, if the transferee repays the debt on behalf of the mortgagor to extinguish the mortgage, the transfer shall be valid. That is, if the transferee exercises the right of elimination (dichu quan) to remove the mortgage encumbrance on the subject matter of transfer, the transfer shall be valid. full_text_en:
Chongqing Suote Salt Chemical Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Xinwanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over land use right transfer contract

Ruling Summary

I. Pursuant to Article 191 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 49 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, during the mortgage period, the mortgagor's transfer of the mortgaged property shall notify the mortgagee and obtain the mortgagee's consent; otherwise, the transfer is invalid. However, Article 191 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 67 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China also provide that where the mortgagor transfers the mortgaged property without notification or consent, if the transferee discharges the debt on behalf of the mortgagor to eliminate the mortgage, the transfer is valid. That is, if the transferee extinguishes the mortgage encumbrance on the subject matter of the transfer by exercising the right of removal, the transfer is valid. The above provisions of the law and judicial interpretation are intended to achieve a balance of interests among the mortgagee, mortgagor, and transferee, ensuring full protection of the mortgage without undue hindrance to the free circulation of property, thereby maximizing the utility of the property.

II. Pursuant to Article 15 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, a contract concluded between parties for the establishment, modification, transfer, or extinguishment of a real property right takes effect upon its formation, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties; failure to register the property right does not affect the validity of the contract. This provision establishes the principle of distinguishing between the cause and the result of a change in real property rights. The failure to effect a transfer of the property right does not necessarily render the contract for the transfer of the property right invalid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 122

Appellant (Defendant at first instance, Counterclaimant): Chongqing Xinwanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Unit 6-1, Building 1, Jinlong Commercial Building, No. 523 Songpai Road, Longxi Street, Yubei District, Chongqing.

Legal Representative: Wen Jingcheng, Chairperson of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Ren Xiuqi, attorney at Beijing Jiuyang Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at first instance, Counterclaim defendant): Chongqing Suote Salt Chemical Co., Ltd., domiciled at Section 3, Shalong Road, Wanzhou District, Chongqing.

Legal Representative: Li Jun, Chairperson of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Zhi, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Han Mei, attorney at Beijing Deheng Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a land use right transfer contract between the appellant Chongqing Xinwanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinwanji Company) and the appellee Chongqing Suote Salt Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Suote Company), the Chongqing High People's Court rendered a civil judgment on July 31, 2008, (2008) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi No. 2. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Xinwanji Company appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel and held a hearing on November 26, 2008. Wen Jingcheng, the legal representative of Xinwanji Company, and its agent ad litem Ren Xiuqi, and Yang Zhi and Han Mei, agents ad litem of Suote Company, appeared before the court. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial: Suote Company held the right to use four parcels of commercial land located at No. 1 Guanyinyan, Wanzhou District, Chongqing, and had mortgaged the said land to relevant banks as loan security, with the mortgage term from 2005 to 2011. On December 1, 2005, Xinwanji Company and Suote Company entered into the "Joint Development Agreement for Golden Three Gorges Garden" (hereinafter referred to as the "Joint Development Agreement") to jointly develop the Golden Three Gorges Garden on the said land. The agreement provided: Article 1, Suote Company had mortgaged the said land to a certain bank for financing loans and agreed to release the mortgage on the land within a specified time. Article 2, the parties would engage in real estate development jointly by way of Xinwanji Company contributing capital and Suote Company contributing the land use right, with joint investment and profit sharing. Article 4, Xinwanji Company undertook to gradually invest development funds as required by the project, with an initial amount of RMB 5 million to be paid within 7 working days from the date of contract execution for preliminary development preparations. Suote Company undertook that the existing mortgage procedures on the land involved in this project would be handled to release the mortgage without affecting the development progress, and guaranteed that there were no other defects in title and that the land had not been sealed up by judicial authorities or restricted by administrative authorities. If a third party claimed any interest in the land, or if the title formalities were incomplete, or if there were any title obstacles, Suote Company would be responsible for resolving them at its own cost, and if this caused losses to Xinwanji Company, Suote Company would bear liability for breach of contract. Article 5, Xinwanji Company would provide all construction funds for the cooperative project of no less than RMB 400 million, and Suote Company would provide all lawfully obtained construction land for the cooperative project. Article 6, Xinwanji Company would upgrade and renovate Suote Company's office building into a four-star hotel, with a renovation cost of RMB 31 million; after renovation, the property rights would belong to Suote Company. Article 9, the buildings and structures on the land would be demolished by Xinwanji Company. Article 10, after the execution of this agreement, if Suote Company breached the agreement by refusing to cooperate with Xinwanji Company, or if, after the project's design was approved by the government, Suote Company failed to cooperate with Xinwanji Company in applying to the government for joint construction, project approval, planning, etc., under the names of both parties, it would be deemed a fundamental breach of contract by Suote Company, and Suote Company would pay liquidated damages to Xinwanji Company equal to 30% of Xinwanji Company's total investment, and compensate for all economic losses caused thereby, including but not limited to preliminary design and back-and-forth negotiation costs; if Xinwanji Company's funds failed to be available in accordance with the development schedule, affecting development, or if Xinwanji Company failed to pay Suote Company's profit on time, Xinwanji Company would pay liquidated damages to Suote Company equal to 30% of the total investment; if work stoppage exceeded 30 days due to project funding issues, in addition to paying liquidated damages to Suote Company, Xinwanji Company would be subject to Suote Company's right to terminate the contract and to seek through legal channels all losses caused thereby.

On December 1, 2005, Xinwanji Company and Suote Company also entered into the "Supplemental Agreement (I) to the Joint Development Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplemental Agreement"). It provided: 1. When the project becomes ready for construction, the parties shall jointly determine the "Golden Three Gorges Garden Joint Development Project Development Schedule," which shall serve as the timetable for Xinwanji Company's development fund availability and Suote Company's cooperation. 2. Regardless of the manner in which the project is developed or the distribution of taxes and fees involved, such taxes and fees shall be borne by Xinwanji Company, and Suote Company shall only receive after-tax profits in accordance with the profit distribution method specified in Article 4 of this Supplemental Agreement. 3. Suote Company's distributed after-tax profits shall be calculated based on the actual land use right delivered to Xinwanji Company for development; the parties agreed to calculate the total profit amount at RMB 370,000 per mu, to be paid by Xinwanji Company to Suote Company in accordance with this article. Suote Company shall not bear any liability for operational risks or losses arising from Xinwanji Company's development of this project. Within one year from the date of execution of this Supplemental Agreement, Xinwanji Company shall pay 30% of the total profit amount to Suote Company; within two years from the date of execution, Xinwanji Company shall pay 40% of the total profit amount; within three years (or upon project completion), Xinwanji Company shall pay the remaining 30% of the total profit amount, and the performance deposit already paid by Xinwanji Company to Suote Company shall be converted into profit and offset against the profit payable by Xinwanji Company to Suote Company. 4. At the start of the project, Xinwanji Company shall upgrade Suote Company's existing office building into a four-star hotel and complete the renovation within one year according to Suote Company's plan; the cost of the renovation, RMB 31 million, shall be borne by Xinwanji Company, and this cost is not within the scope of the profit payable by Xinwanji Company to Suote Company under Article 4 of this Supplemental Agreement. 5. This Supplemental Agreement is a valid appendix to the Joint Development Agreement; in the event of any conflict with the Joint Development Agreement, this Supplemental Agreement shall prevail.

On December 5, 2005, Xinwanji Company sent Suote Company the "Golden Three Gorges Garden Joint Development Project Development Schedule (I)" stating that in order to facilitate the smooth progress of various tasks, Suote Company was requested to cooperate in completing the preliminary project development within the corresponding time frame, including handling the land mortgage release procedures before January 20, 2006, and requested Suote Company to confirm and reply. Suote Company did not reply.

On December 25, 2005, Xinwanji Company entered into the "Construction Engineering Design Contract (I)" with CISDI Engineering Technology Co., Ltd., stipulating that Xinwanji Company commissioned CISDI Engineering Technology Co., Ltd. to design the Golden Three Gorges Garden City, with a design fee calculated at RMB 22 per square meter, provisionally estimated at RMB 11 million. After the contract was signed, CISDI Engineering Technology Co., Ltd. produced a design plan and design renderings.

On December 25, 2005, Xinwanji Company entered into the "Personnel Secondment Agreement" with Chongqing Suote (Group) Co., Ltd. Tourism Company (hereinafter referred to as Suote Tourism Company). It provided that in order to coordinate with the progress of the joint development project between Xinwanji Company and Suote Company, the Suote Hotel had officially ceased operations; to properly resolve the employment arrangement for Suote Tourism Company's employees during the project construction transition period, Suote Tourism Company would second 17 employees to Xinwanji Company in the form of a secondment, and Xinwanji Company would pay the seconded personnel their remuneration, social insurance, and welfare benefits in accordance with labor law provisions. On March 10, 2006, Xinwanji Company paid wages totaling RMB 18,980 to 17 employees including Wang Youmin and Hong Jiang.

In December 2005, Xinwanji Company entered into two "Loan Agreements" with Suote Tourism Company, stipulating that Xinwanji Company would lend RMB 1.5 million to Suote Tourism Company.

From December 25, 2005, Xinwanji Company repeatedly sent letters to Suote Company, requesting Suote Company to fulfill its obligations of cooperation in the development of the Golden Three Gorges Garden project.

On January 4, 2006, Xinwanji Company entered into the "Chongqing Xinwanji Real Estate 'Wanzhou Guanyinyan' Project Full-Process Development Consultant and Marketing Agency Contract" with Chengdu Shangzhu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. Xinwanji Company commissioned Chengdu Shangzhu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. to serve as the "full-process development consultant and marketing agent" for the Golden Three Gorges project, with the agency fee calculated at 2.2% of the total sales amount of this project. After the contract was signed, Chengdu Shangzhu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. provided Xinwanji Company with a "Service Plan."

On March 6, 2006, China Construction Bank Chongqing Wanzhou Branch sent a letter to Suote Company stating that Suote Company, without the bank's consent, unilaterally cooperated with others in real estate development using the mortgaged property, seriously infringing upon the bank's mortgage rights, and demanded that Suote Company immediately cease the infringing conduct.

On April 10, 2006, Xinwanji Company entered into the "Building Demolition Contract" with Yang Tiange, stipulating that Yang Tiange would undertake the demolition of above-ground structures and removal of debris within the scope of the Golden Three Gorges Garden project. On April 12, 2007, Xinwanji Company and Yang Tiange entered into the "Golden Three Gorges Development Project Demolition Supplemental Agreement." The agreement stated that because Xinwanji Company failed to fulfill its promise to start construction in June 2006, causing Yang Tiange to suffer certain economic losses, the parties agreed to make certain modifications to the "Building Demolition Contract" dated April 10, 2006.

On December 29, 2005, Xinwanji Company paid RMB 20,000 to the Wanzhou District Real Estate Administration of Chongqing as "housing fair participation fee." On April 25, 2006, Xinwanji Company paid RMB 40,340.5 to Chengdu Kangmei Kaixin Advertising Co., Ltd. as "2006 Wanzhou Housing Fair Exhibition Stand Design and Decoration Construction Fee."

On December 20, 2007, Suote Company filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing High People's Court, alleging that after entering into the "Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" with Xinwanji Company, Xinwanji Company failed to perform its corresponding obligations in accordance with the contract, rendering the joint construction work impossible and the purpose of joint development unattainable. Accordingly, Suote Company requested the court to: 1. Rescind the "Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" entered into by the parties; 2. Order Xinwanji Company to pay liquidated damages of RMB 10 million to Suote Company; 3. Order Xinwanji Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Xinwanji Company argued in its defense: After the contracts were signed, Xinwanji Company actively performed its own obligations, but Suote Company refused to perform its contractual obligations on various pretexts, causing the joint construction work to stall. Therefore, Xinwanji Company requested the court to dismiss Suote Company's claims.

Xinwanji Company filed a counterclaim, alleging: After the "Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" were signed, Xinwanji Company actively carried out preliminary development work and repeatedly urged Suote Company to perform its contractual obligations, but Suote Company has still failed to perform its principal contractual obligations to date. In addition, due to the appreciation of the land price involved in the project, Suote Company, in an attempt to monopolize the project benefits, attempted to breach the contract on various excuses. Accordingly, Xinwanji Company requested the court to: 1. Order Suote Company to pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million to Xinwanji Company; 2. Order Suote Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Suote Company argued in response to Xinwanji Company's counterclaim: According to the contract, Xinwanji Company was required to first perform its payment obligation and provide a government-approved plan before it could demand that Suote Company perform its corresponding cooperation obligations. However, Xinwanji Company has not performed the above obligations to date; therefore, Xinwanji Company's counterclaim is unfounded and should be dismissed.

The court of first instance held that: (A) The nature of the legal relationship between the parties. Pursuant to Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over State-Owned Land Use Right Contracts, a cooperative real estate development contract is characterized by joint investment, profit sharing, and risk sharing. In this case, the "Joint Development Agreement" did not expressly stipulate the allocation of benefits and risks in the development of the Golden Three Gorges Garden project; rather, it was provided for in the "Supplemental Agreement." Viewed from the rights and obligations determined in Articles 4 and 5 of the "Supplemental Agreement," in the project development, Suote Company's primary obligation was to provide the land and cooperate with Xinwanji Company's development activities, while the benefits it obtained included a consideration of RMB 103.6 million (calculated at RMB 370,000 per mu x 280 mu) and an office building renovation valued at RMB 31 million; Suote Company did not bear the operational risks of the project. Therefore, the legal relationship between the parties lacked the element of risk sharing and did not constitute a cooperative real estate development contract in legal nature. From the specific content of these rights and obligations, Suote Company was to receive a fixed amount of consideration upon providing the right to use the land in question, which in substance amounted to a transfer of the land use right, i.e., Suote Company was the transferor of the land and Xinwanji Company was the transferee.

(B) The legal validity of the transfer. The transfer of the land use right violated legal provisions and should be held invalid. First, Article 49(1) of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Security Law") provides: "During the mortgage period, a mortgagor who transfers the registered mortgaged property shall notify the mortgagee and inform the transferee that the property is mortgaged; if the mortgagor fails to notify the mortgagee or inform the transferee, the transfer is invalid." In this case, there was no evidence that Suote Company notified the China Construction Bank and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of the transfer; according to the above provision, the transfer should be held invalid. Second, Article 67(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Security Law Interpretation") provides: "During the existence of the mortgage, if the mortgagor transfers the mortgaged property without notifying the mortgagee or informing the transferee, and if the mortgaged property is registered, the mortgagee may still exercise the mortgage right; the transferee who has obtained ownership of the mortgaged property may, in lieu of the debtor, discharge all of the debtor's debts, thereby extinguishing the mortgage. After discharging the debt, the transferee may seek recourse against the mortgagor." Since the subject matter transferred to Xinwanji Company was encumbered with a mortgage, according to this provision, Xinwanji Company could remedy the validity of the transfer by exercising the right of removal to extinguish the mortgage, but Xinwanji Company did not exercise the right of removal, and thus the validity of the transfer could not be remedied. Suote Company's request to rescind the "Joint Development Agreement" and its "Supplemental Agreement" entered into by the parties could not be granted. The so-called rescission of a contract is to extinguish the legal effect of a lawful and valid contract, whereas the "Joint Development Agreement" and its "Supplemental Agreement" were invalid contracts; therefore, there was no issue of rescission.

(3) Legal Liability for the Invalid Transfer. Pursuant to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law"), the legal consequences of an invalid contract are the return of property and compensation for losses. In this case, there was no delivery or transfer of property between the parties, so there is no issue of return. As for losses, New Wanji Company, in performing the contract, paid wages of RMB 18,980 to 17 employees of Suote Tourism Company, paid an exhibition participation fee of RMB 20,000 to the Real Estate Administration Bureau of Wanzhou District, Chongqing, and paid booth design, renovation, and construction fees of RMB 40,340.5 to Chengdu Kangmei Kaixin Advertising Co., Ltd., totaling RMB 79,320.5. The above amounts are losses suffered by New Wanji Company due to performance of the contract, and the liability for compensation shall be determined according to the fault of the parties. Looking at the reason for the invalidity of the contract in this case, it was the failure to notify the mortgagee of the land transfer. Pursuant to Article 49, paragraph 1 of the Security Law, the obligation to give such notice should be performed by the mortgagor. Therefore, it was the sole fault of Suote Company that led to the invalidity of the contract, and Suote Company shall bear the liability to compensate New Wanji Company for the losses suffered as a result. Although according to Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law, the transferee may also extinguish the mortgage by exercising the right of elimination, thereby making the transfer effective, for the transferee, this provision confers a right. If the transferee, as the right holder, does not exercise the right, this does not constitute legal fault. New Wanji Company argued that it had entered into a Loan Agreement with Suote Tourism Company and lent RMB 1.43 million, which were expenses incurred for performing the contract. Since it was a loan, the borrower is obligated to repay it, and New Wanji Company has the right to demand repayment from the borrower. Therefore, the loan amount agreed in that agreement should not be regarded as a loss suffered by New Wanji Company. New Wanji Company claimed that it had entered into a Construction Project Design Contract (I) with CISDI Engineering Co., Ltd. and paid design fees of RMB 4.4 million; it had entered into a Full-Process Development Advisory and Marketing Agency Contract for the "Chongqing New Wanji Base 'Wanzhou Guanyinyan'" Project with Chengdu Shangzhu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. and paid planning agency fees of RMB 1.15 million; and it had entered into a House Demolition Contract and a Demolition Supplementary Agreement for the Jin Sanxia Development Project with Yang Tiange, and failure to perform the contract would result in corresponding liability for breach of contract. The authenticity of the above contracts and payments can be examined in separate proceedings. Even if the contracts and payments are genuine and valid, because the Joint Development Agreement and its Supplementary Agreement are invalid, the above four contracts cannot be performed further. For such contracts that have not been fully performed, when determining their legal consequences, consideration must be given to both the performed part and the unperformed part, and the liability for breach of contract shall be determined based on the parties' default. Therefore, the expenses already paid by New Wanji Company do not equal the losses it suffered. Currently, the legal consequences of these four contracts have not been finally determined, so the losses suffered by New Wanji Company cannot be established. Only after New Wanji Company's liability under the above contracts is determined can the People's Court, based on the different natures of the losses, consider the cause of occurrence, the controlling entity, the degree of controllability, and the fault of both parties to determine the proportion of sharing between New Wanji Company and Suote Company. Based on this, this case does not address this portion of losses. New Wanji Company claimed that it had entered into a House Lease Contract with Zhang Jianhua and paid rent of RMB 237,000; entered into an Office Decoration Contract with Li Guo and paid decoration fees of RMB 150,000; and purchased office furniture and office supplies, incurring expenses of RMB 313,334. The evidence presented by New Wanji Company cannot prove the connection between these expenses and the "Jin Sanxia Garden" project, i.e., it cannot be determined that these expenses were incurred for developing the "Jin Sanxia Garden" project. Therefore, this portion of expenses claimed by New Wanji Company is not supported. New Wanji Company's claimed expenses for transportation, travel, entertainment, etc., are not supported due to lack of evidence.

(4) Liability for Breach of Contract Claimed by Both Parties. In the main action, Suote Company requested that New Wanji Company pay liquidated damages of RMB 10 million. In the counterclaim, New Wanji Company requested that Suote Company pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million. Neither of these claims can be sustained. Liquidated damages fall within the scope of liability for breach of contract, which is a legal liability arising from the breach of a valid contract and is based on the existence of a lawful and valid contractual relationship. In this case, the Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement are invalid, so there is no issue of breach of contract, nor does it give rise to liability for breach of contract.

In summary, based on Article 49, paragraph 1 of the Security Law, Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law, and Article 58 of the Contract Law, the court of first instance ruled as follows: (1) The Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement are invalid; (2) Within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, Suote Company shall compensate New Wanji Company for losses of RMB 79,320.5; (3) Suote Company's claims are dismissed; (4) New Wanji Company's counterclaim is dismissed.

New Wanji Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The first instance judgment erred in law by finding that the land use right transfer contract signed by the parties was invalid. According to Article 67 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law and Article 191 of the Property Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Property Law"), the transfer of mortgaged property without notifying the mortgagee is not automatically invalid. In this case, the parties agreed that Suote Company would first discharge the mortgage on the transferred land, which could protect the interests of the mortgagee. This agreement does not violate mandatory legal provisions, and the transfer contract should be valid. 2. After the contract was signed, despite repeated urgings by New Wanji Company, Suote Company delayed in performing its prior obligation to discharge the mortgage on the transferred land and took the initiative to file a lawsuit to seek the huge benefits from the land appreciation, which is contrary to good faith. New Wanji Company actively invested in performance and suffered huge economic losses. Suote Company should bear liability for breach of contract for this. 3. Suote Company should pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million as stipulated in the contract. Therefore, the appeal requests: 1. To set aside the first instance judgment; 2. To find that the Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement signed by the parties are valid; 3. To find that Suote Company breached the contract and shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million; 4. To order Suote Company to bear all litigation costs.

Suote Company argued in its defense: 1. The contracts involved in this case are invalid because they violate the mandatory provisions of the Security Law. 2. The parties' agreement did not specify the time for Suote Company to discharge the mortgage. Because New Wanji Company failed to invest the initial capital of RMB 5 million and subsequent funds within 7 days of the contract signing as agreed, Suote Company was unable to repay the bank loan and thus could not exercise the discharge of the mortgage with the bank. Therefore, it can be seen that Suote Company did not breach the contract; rather, New Wanji Company breached the contract. 3. The liquidated damages clause can only apply if the contract is valid. Since the contract is invalid in this case, New Wanji Company's claim for RMB 60 million in liquidated damages under that clause is unfounded. In summary, the first instance judgment had lawful procedures, clear factual findings, and correct application of law, and should be affirmed.

The court of second instance found during the retrial: The land transfer price agreed in the Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement signed by the parties on December 1, 2005, was confirmed by the parties to be RMB 480,000 per mu. In February 2008, when Suote Company again mortgaged the relevant land to the bank, its appraised value was approximately RMB 880,000 per mu.

Other facts found by the court of second instance are consistent with the basic facts found by the court of first instance.

Based on the parties' appeal requests and defenses, the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) The validity of the Joint Development Agreement and its Supplementary Agreement. (2) Whether Suote Company should pay liquidated damages to New Wanji Company.

(1) Regarding the validity of the Joint Development Agreement and its Supplementary Agreement. First, according to Article 49 of the Security Law, during the mortgage period, the mortgagor shall notify the mortgagee when transferring the mortgaged property; otherwise, the transfer is invalid. Article 191 of the Property Law also provides that the transfer of mortgaged property during the mortgage period requires the consent of the mortgagee. The legislative purpose of these provisions is to ensure that the interests of the mortgagee are not infringed upon. However, Article 67 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law and Article 191 of the Property Law also provide that if the mortgaged property is transferred without notification or without the consent of the mortgagee, the transfer is valid if the transferee pays off the debt on behalf of the mortgagor to extinguish the mortgage. That is, if the transferee exercises the right of elimination to remove the mortgage burden on the subject matter of the transfer, the transfer is valid. The above provisions of the law and judicial interpretations reflect the guiding principle of relevant legislation and judicial interpretations to achieve a balance of interests among the mortgagee, the mortgagor, and the third party transferee of the mortgaged property, fully protecting the mortgage from infringement without unduly hindering the free transfer of property and fully realizing the utility of the property. In this case, the parties agreed in the Joint Development Agreement that Suote Company would handle the procedures for discharging the mortgage without affecting the development progress, thereby imposing on Suote Company, by agreement, the obligation to first remove the mortgage burden on the land involved in this case. This agreement protects the interests of the mortgagee and does not harm the interests of the mortgagor or the third party transferee of the land, and is not inconsistent with the legislative spirit of the Security Law, the Property Law, and the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law to safeguard the balance of interests of all parties, nor does it violate legal provisions. From the perspective of contract law, the transferor bears a warranty obligation against defects in title to the subject matter of the transfer. Its voluntary disclosure of the rights burden on the transferred land and its commitment to first discharge the mortgage without affecting the development progress constitute a burden-bearing act under the contract, i.e., an act of assuming obligations, which conforms to the principles of autonomy of will and freedom of contract, and ensures that the interests of the mortgagee are not infringed upon. It does not conflict with the legislative intent and institutional design of the Security Law, the Property Law, and the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law. Therefore, the Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement should be confirmed as valid, the parties should perform diligently in accordance with the contracts, and Suote Company is obliged to repay the bank debt based on the development schedule agreed upon by the parties, thereby discharging the mortgage burden on the transferred land.

Second, according to Article 15 of the Property Law, a contract concluded between the parties concerning the creation, modification, transfer, or extinction of a real right in immovable property shall become effective upon the formation of the contract, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties; the failure to register the real right does not affect the validity of the contract. This provision establishes the principle of distinguishing between the cause and the result of changes in real rights in immovable property. The failure to achieve the transfer of real rights does not necessarily render the cause of the transfer of real rights, i.e., the obligatory contract, invalid. The Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement signed by the parties, as the causal act for the transfer of the land use rights in dispute, constitute an act of creating obligatory rights, not an act of changing the real rights for the transfer of the land use rights. The provision of relevant laws that the failure to notify the mortgagee renders the act of transferring real rights invalid should not extend its effect to the causal act of the change in real rights. This is because the parties can perfect the conditions for the transfer of real rights in their contractual agreements, making the transfer comply with legal requirements. This case falls under such circumstances.

In summary, the Joint Development Agreement signed by the parties does not violate mandatory legal provisions and should be a valid contract. The first instance judgment's finding on this issue applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected.

(2) Whether Suote Company should pay liquidated damages to New Wanji Company. The first instance judgment determined that the parties' agreement was a land use right transfer agreement based on the rights and obligations agreed in the Joint Development Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement. This factual finding is clear, and the application of law is correct. Both parties have no objection, and this Court affirms it. As a bilateral contract, a land use right transfer agreement requires the transferor to first provide land with unencumbered use rights, and the transferee to pay the transfer price in accordance with the agreement. Article 1 of the parties' Joint Development Agreement explicitly states that the transferred land is mortgaged and stipulates that Suote Company shall perform the obligation to discharge the mortgage. This stipulation indicates that Suote Company, as the transferor of the land use rights, has the obligation to remove the existing rights defects on the transferred land. In the subsequently signed Supplementary Agreement, the parties agreed on the time for performing their respective obligations, using the jointly determined "Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Project Development Schedule" as the timetable for the parties to perform their obligations. In accordance with the Supplementary Agreement, New Wanji Company submitted the "Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Project Development Schedule" to Suote Company on December 5, 2005, requesting Suote Company to discharge the mortgage on the transferred land. Suote Company did not respond. This action by Suote Company violated the obligatory provision in Article 1 of the Joint Development Agreement regarding the parties jointly determining the project development schedule, and failed to timely discharge the mortgage set on the transferred land as agreed, failing to provide land with unencumbered rights. This passive failure to perform the contract constitutes a breach of contract. Suote Company's silence gave rise to New Wanji Company's legitimate expectation that the contract would continue to be performed, leading New Wanji Company to enter into contracts for engineering design and a series of other acts related to project development and implementation with third parties such as CISDI Engineering Co., Ltd. Under these circumstances, Suote Company filed a lawsuit requesting the rescission of the Joint Development Contract and the Supplementary Agreement. According to Article 108 of the Contract Law, this should be deemed a fundamental breach of contract. Suote Company argued that its failure to discharge the mortgage was because New Wanji Company failed to pay the transfer price, leaving it without funds to discharge the mortgage. According to Article 4 of the Joint Development Agreement, Suote Company's commitment, Suote Company should use its own funds to perform the obligation to discharge the mortgage, not conditional on New Wanji Company's prior payment of the transfer price. Therefore, Suote Company's defense is untenable. In summary, considering the significant appreciation of the land involved and the balance of interests between the parties in the land use right transfer process, Suote Company shall bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with Article 10 of the Joint Development Agreement. According to that article, Suote Company's fundamental breach of contract requires it to pay liquidated damages equal to 30% of New Wanji Company's total investment amount. Since the Joint Development Agreement signed by the parties is in fact a land use right transfer agreement, the "total investment amount" stipulated in that article should be changed to the amount of the transfer price agreed in the contract, to be used as the basis for calculating liability for breach of contract. According to the Supplementary Agreement, the parties determined that Suote Company's entitled proceeds from the transfer of the land use rights were RMB 103.6 million (280 mu x RMB 370,000/mu), and New Wanji Company was to bear the cost of decorating Suote Company's office building amounting to RMB 31 million; as the consideration for the transfer of land use rights, the total of the two items was RMB 134.6 million. Based on this calculation, Suote Company shall pay New Wanji Company liquidated damages of RMB 40.38 million. New Wanji Company's request, based on the total investment amount it planned to invest in development, that Suote Company should pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million is premised on a cooperative development arrangement, which is inconsistent with the facts of this case, and this Court does not support it. Given that New Wanji Company believes that Suote Company's failure to perform its contractual obligations constitutes a fundamental breach of contract, and this Court also confirms this, and Suote Company requested in the first instance to rescind the contracts signed by the parties, the Joint Development Agreement and its Supplementary Agreement signed by the parties should be rescinded. New Wanji Company argued during the proceedings that it had actually paid relevant expenses to perform the agreement and requested this Court to confirm them. Since this claim was not part of its claim in the first instance, and the liquidated damages payable by Suote Company already exceed that claim, this Court does not support this claim in the second instance.

This Court holds that the Joint Development Agreement and its Supplementary Agreement signed by the parties represent the true intention of the parties, do not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and are lawful and valid. Suote Company's failure to perform its contractual obligations constitutes a breach of contract and shall bear liability for breach of contract as agreed in the contract. New Wanji Company's grounds of appeal are partially well-founded, and this Court supports them. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2008) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Chongqing High People's Court is set aside;
2. The "Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement (I) to the Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Agreement" are valid;
3. The "Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement (I) to the Jin Sanxia Garden Joint Development Agreement" signed by the parties are rescinded;
4. Chongqing Suote Salt and Chemical Co., Ltd. shall pay Chongqing New Wanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. liquidated damages of RMB 40.38 million within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment;
5. The other appeal requests of Chongqing New Wanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the pecuniary obligation to pay as determined in this judgment is not performed within the period specified, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 304,900; counterclaim fee: RMB 170,900; total: RMB 475,800. Chongqing Suote Salt and Chemical Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 350,694; Chongqing New Wanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 125,106.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 170,900. Chongqing Suote Salt and Chemical Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 112,794; Chongqing New Wanji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 58,106.

This judgment is final.
